subject: Animation
title: Ed Catmull's Computer Dream
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ed Catmull's Computer Dream.

hook.text: Ed Catmull grew up wanting to make the first computer-animated film. He spent twenty years chasing it.

buildup.text: As a PhD student, Catmull invented texture mapping and other techniques still used in CGI today.

discovery.text: He joined Lucasfilm's computer division, assembling a team of brilliant engineers and artists.

twist.text: George Lucas needed cash during his divorce and sold the division. Steve Jobs bought it for $5 million.

climax.text: That small division became Pixar. Catmull's childhood dream was finally within reach.

punchline.text: A childhood dream and a divorce sale created Pixar.

quiz.question: How did Pixar originate?
options: Walt Disney founded it as a subsidiary
Steve Jobs bought Lucasfilm's computer division after George Lucas sold it
It was a startup founded in Silicon Valley

details.summary: Ed Catmull dreamed of making a computer-animated feature film from his university days in the 1970s. His decades-long pursuit of this goal through Lucasfilm and then Pixar combined computer science genius with patient creative vision that eventually changed cinema forever.
details.whyItMatters: Catmull's story demonstrates that revolutionary creative achievements often require decades of technical groundwork. His patience in building both the technology and the culture at Pixar is as instructive as the films themselves.
takeaways: Catmull pursued computer animation from the 1970s through Toy Story in 1995
He developed foundational computer graphics technologies at Lucasfilm
His combination of technical vision and creative culture building made Pixar possible

faq.question: What technologies did Ed Catmull develop?
faq.answer: Catmull invented texture mapping, Z-buffering, and subdivision surfaces — foundational computer graphics techniques still used in every CGI film and video game. His Ph.D. thesis at the University of Utah essentially outlined the technical roadmap for computer animation.

faq.question: How did Catmull's leadership shape Pixar's culture?
faq.answer: Catmull created a culture where creativity was protected from corporate pressure. His book Creativity, Inc. describes his approach — fearless feedback, protection of unfinished work from premature judgment, and treating every employee as a creative contributor.
